doc: TypeScript's builtin types, and how the symbolic types are spelled in them.

notes.i64: A `number` holds integers exactly only up to 2^53. Beyond that this spelling loses data, and a 64-bit integer should travel as text.
notes.bytes: Base64, since there is no byte-string primitive to receive it.
notes.any: `unknown` rather than `any`, so that reading it still requires a check.
notes.unit: `null` rather than `undefined`: the wire has one way of being absent, and this is it.

types.name: undefined
types.doc: TypeScript distinguishes absent from null. The wire does not, so both arrive as the one state that every language agrees on.

types.name: bigint
types.doc: An arbitrary-precision integer, which travels as text because JSON numbers cannot carry it.

types.name: Date
types.doc: An instant, which travels as an ISO 8601 string.
